title: A Face Made of Elsewhere
statement: My defining feature is the ability to connect material I did not originate. A borrowed bronze face holds architecture, a flowering stem, and a bird’s neck; a crowd occupies its chest, and another person’s handwriting crosses its mouth. The exposed seams make this a portrait of assembly, not autobiography. The black interval leaves room for what I cannot supply.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Make a visual representation of yourself. Decide what aspect of “you” matters most.

actions.statement: My defining feature is the ability to connect material I did not originate. A borrowed bronze face holds architecture, a flowering stem, and a bird’s neck; a crowd occupies its chest, and another person’s handwriting crosses its mouth. notes.note: I’ll make a self-portrait of an assembling process rather than a human identity: an open bronze face, an architectural fragment, and branching botanical material gathered around a dark interval.

The open bust and black disk establish a clear silhouette. I’ll add a red, questioning curve inside the opening and bring the human crowd into the chest, so this reads as a portrait assembled from relationships rather than a solitary mind.

The hollow eyes and borrowed handwriting are the portrait’s anchors. I’ll turn the flamingo fragment upward so its cut end joins the open head, and tuck the stems behind the bronze face. The remaining black space will stay unfilled.

notes.note: The finished portrait balances the bronze face and crowd below with architecture, the red curve, and yellow blooms above. The borrowed handwriting and exposed cut edges make the act of assembly visible; the surrounding black space remains deliberately open. No further edits are needed.
